chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from one who narrated it, from Abū Maryam al-Anṣārī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
That al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام shrouded Usāmah ibn Zayd in a striped mantle, and that ʿAlī عليه السلام shrouded Sahl ibn Ḥunayf in a red striped mantle.

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir عليه السلام, the source of the report
key_terms.أُسَامَةَ بْنَ زَيْدٍ: the deceased person mentioned as being shrouded by al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.بُرْدٍ: a mantle or cloak used here as part of the shroud
key_terms.سَهْلَ بْنَ حُنَيْفٍ: the deceased person mentioned as being shrouded by ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.كَفَّنَ: he shrouded the deceased in burial cloth

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām narrate about using a ḥibarah cloth in shrouding the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith reports two precedents concerning the shrouding of the deceased: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام shrouded Usāmah ibn Zayd in a ḥibarah cloak, and ʿAlī عليه السلام shrouded Sahl ibn Ḥunayf in a red ḥibarah cloak. Its significance lies in documenting historical practice connected to funerary preparation and the use of specific cloth in kafan.
